GB Logistics Commerce Ltd trades at an exceptionally low price-to-earnings multiple of just 4.87x based on filed statements [E1], or 8.39x against a sector benchmark of 19.94x [E6]. This profound disconnect is further underscored by a price-to-book ratio of 0.48x, with the stock priced at ₹ 27.0 against a book value of ₹ 56.6 [E2], alongside an even lower provider-reported P/B of 0.44x versus a sector benchmark of 1.51x [E7]. Compounding this deep asset and earnings discount, the business generates a solid ROCE of 15.2% [E10] and boasts an impressive historical track record, including a 3-year median return on equity of 20% [E18] and a 5-year median return on equity reaching 22% [E17]. The market has pushed the stock down to sit merely 7% of the way up its 52-week range [E5], presenting an extreme divergence between fundamental earning power and current valuation. Conceded: [E4].

Conceded: [E1], [E2], [E6], [E7], [E17], and [E18]. While the bull highlights low valuation multiples like a 4.87x P/E [E1] and 0.48x price-to-book [E2], these discounts are a direct reflection of structural value destruction, evidenced by the stock languishing merely 7% of the way up its 52-week range between a low of 24 and a high of 67 [E5]. Furthermore, historical profitability metrics are in a sharp downward trend, with the 5-year median ROE of 22% [E17] and 3-year median ROE of 20% [E18] collapsing down to a current ROE of only 12% [E19]. This severe contraction in returns completely undermines the sustainability of past earnings power [E17, E18, E19]. Compounding this deteriorating fundamental outlook, the company returns zero capital to its shareholders, paying a dividend yield of exactly 0.00% [E4]. Consequently, investors buying these discounted assets receive neither cash distributions [E4] nor stability against a plunging share price [E5].
